DISCUSSION
The Reset-Set (RS) flip-flop is designed to store the last input condition until the next input condition is applied.
The RS flip-flop has two inputs and two outputs.
A high applied to the SET (S) input sets the output Q high and output Q low.
A high applied to the RESET (R) input sets output Q low and the output Q high.
If a high is applied to inputs S and R at the same time an illegal state exists. The outputs Q and Q cannot be determined. v
An application for the RS flip-flop is as a replacement for the mechanical switch.
Mechanical switches physically vibrate or bounce several times before a solid contact is made.
Bouncing of the switch causes voltage spikes that can effect digital circuit operation.
The RS flip-flop acts as an electrical switch. There is no mechanical bounce produced by the flip-flop.
When does this RS flip-flop produce a high output on Q?
When a high is applied to the R or reset input of a flip-flop the Q output goes low and the Q output goes high.

This RS flip-flop is constructed from two NOR gates. RS
flip-flops can also be constructed from NAND gates.
Let's start with a high applied to input S and a low applied to input R. The output Q is high and output Q is low.
The high input on S is applied to gate B and inverted to a low output. Any high input to a NOR gate will produce a low output.
The output of gate B is used as a feedback signal to the input of gate A.
The low input on R is applied to gate A. The two low inputs of gate A are inverted producing a high output on Q.
The output of gate A is used as a feedback signal to the input of gate B.
Notice, even if the inputs are removed the feedback signal
from gate A will hold the Q output low. Remember, any high input produces a low output.
The flip-flop must remain in the set state until a high is applied to the reset input.
When a high is applied to the R input and a low is applied to the S input the gate will reset.
The high input on R is applied to gate A and inverted to a low output.
The output of gate A is used as a feedback to the input of gate B.
The low input on S is applied to gate B. The two low inputs to gate B are inverted producing a high output on Q.
The output of gate B is used as a feedback to the input of gate A.
Notice, even if the inputs are removed the feedback signal from gate B will hold the Q output low.
The flip-flop must remain in the reset state until a high is applied to the set input.
Feedback allows the flip-flop to hold the last input condition until a different condition is applied.
The ability of the flip-flop to hold an output condition, even after the inputs have been removed, is a result of feedback.

Now let's look at the RS flip-flop operation when constructed using NAND gates.
If the S input goes low while the R input is held high the flip-flop will go to a SET state.
The low on the S input is applied to gate A and inverted to a high output. Any low input to a NAND gate will produce a high output.
The output of gate A is used as a feedback signal to the input of gate B.
The high on the R input is applied to gate B. The two high inputs on gate B are inverted due to the NAND function and provide a low output.
Notice, when the S input goes back to its high resting state at t1 the output does not change.
The flip-flop will remain in the SET state until there is a low on the R input and a high on the S input.
When the S input is held high with the R input going low the output will RESET.
The low applied to gate B will be inverted by the NAND gate to provide a high on the Q output.
The high output of gate B is fed back to the input of gate A.
With a high applied to the S input and the high provided by the feedback signal the output of gate A is low.
Notice at t1, when the R input goes back to its high resting state the output does not change.
The flip-flop will remain in the reset state until there is a low on the S input and a high on the R input.
The operation of the flip-flop can be summarized using a truth table.
Notice that it is the low on the S input OR low on the R input that provides the SET or RESET states. This indicates that the flip-flop is active low.
